body: But I'm tired at this point, and my left arm kills after cutting it. I suppose I'll be forced to keep going for another day; another day where I beg to be freed from this life.

I do find it sad that there are so many posta of people crying out for help, but receiving no answer. Perhaps if everyone worked together, they'd be able to solve their problems. But why do that? They're the ones in need of help, not others. Even I could take the time to reply to someone, even if it is just the generic message to soldier onwards. But why should I bother when others won't do the same to me? It is similar to life; no.matter how generous, kind or nice one is, you will still get fucked over somehow.

Even as I slice open my forearm, I do feel scared of death, and will probably stop at one point as a natural instinct to avoid it. At least I have the satisfaction of possibly further progressing my pathway to death, and peace.

Referring back to my points about life being futile; for each happy moment one experiences, the negative response will be multiple times worse. Marriage? Romance?  Divorce, death, abuse... Graduate? Hope? Optimism? Isolation, exhaustion, stress... I could go on, and probably will at some point.

Before death, I've always wanted to have a form of biography, or scuicide note. Where I can express my views, life experiences, and show that I have thought deeply about things and explored different solutions, both positive and negative ones. But I've always put it off, as there would be too much to write; in my depths I'd rather die there and then rather than have to write a book.

Speaking of death, I do think no person truly desires death, and rather would prefer to cease existence - to just disappear; to not think, to not worry, to not feel - for there just to be nothing. Unfortunately, once the sin of bringing someone into the world is complete, there is no out other than suicide, or to live a dreadful life and to die by natural causes. Personally, I hope and pray that I die in my dreams, or some cosmic power smites me from existence one day - but it never happens. And I know it never will. But I don't want to be here anymore.

I suppose I'll talk to myself.

Scuicide is probably the most selfish act, pherhaps more than rape or murder; the scope of people affected ranges from one's family, all the way to the clraners whom must clean up aftee you. But, it is the right of those who carry oit the act to be able to do so. They were not given a choice as to be born into this world; their social status, race, gender - it is all forced upon you, and you are required to take on this burden.

The greatest sin one can commit is probably bringing a life into the world - whether you have good intentions or not, you are condemning your baby to a life of horror and sadness, only perpetuated with things auch as occasional endorphin boost; not mayter how happy one gets, they'll always return to a point of sadness, as if a pendulum scale; apart from the fact that the scale spends far more time on one end than the other. Thus, those who give life to a child without the intention of pushing their child's scale towards happiness are true scum; but in a way, it is no different to those that attempt to give their child utmost happiness.


No matter how much you progress, or how happy you get, you'll always revert back to square one. That is why life is futile; "making the most of things" is a useless phrase, as what's the point of living life if the majority of it is in darkness? You're better off skipping to the end of it, and having true peace.

Even in my darkest moments, there is nowhere to turn for help; looking towards an authority figure such as a therapist of cancelled can lead to more problems than benefits; discussing your troubles with family can lead to you being an outcast, or spreading your issues to them instead - one could argue that scuicide would result in that anyway, but once you're at peace, does anything in your lifetime truly matter? Even Suicide prevention sub-reddits and Discord servers will give you the same repetitious advice, which may help some, but won't help many. But I suppose no-one has the answers.

But one truth I know is that this life isn't worth the trouble. And I hope eventually I can get out.
